title: TUI relay board animates running relays
lead: A board in the TUI shows each active relay run as a lane: the slice, the worktree, and the role pipeline `implementer ▸ reviewer ▸ gate` (architect when present). Each role shows its agent, vendor, model, reasoning, task, elapsed time and subagent count, and an ASCII spinner marks the active step. The board refreshes on a timer while it is open.
findings_note: owner request, session 2026-10-14: monitor slice relays from the TUI
boundary: **Not in this slice:** starting, stopping or steering a run. The board is read-only. Showing slivers under their parent waits for s273's `parent` field; until then, each sliver is its own lane.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The owner asked for a visual, animated view of the relays in flight. s282 supplies the data. The TUI input loop blocks on `screen.get_wch()` (`src/slicer/tui.py:1157`), so it cannot animate today.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/tui.py`: a `board` mode and binding. A pure `board_lines(runs, tick, now, width)` returns the lanes, with the spinner frame chosen by `tick`, so tests need no terminal. `run()` sets `screen.timeout(ms)` only while the board is open, feeding a `tick` key to `View.handle`, and keeps blocking input otherwise. Stale runs are dimmed and labelled `stale`. Uses `tui_style` roles for colour, with a monochrome fallback.
- `docs/tui.md` (a Relay board section), `CHANGELOG.md`, `tests/test_tui.py`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and watch them go red.
2. Add `board_lines`, the mode and the tick handling; then the timed poll in `run()`.
3. Update the docs and CHANGELOG.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- The affected tests, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.
- By hand: record a fake run with `relay-run begin/step` and watch `slicer tui` animate it, then end it and see the lane leave the active board.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/s283`, branch `feature/s283-tui-relay-board`. Commit only on the branch.
